findings.issue: rel_or_abs(mp10, os.getcwd()) returns the ABSOLUTE path whenever scratch and cwd are on different drives, which is exactly the hosted windows runner (checkout on D:, scratch on C:). i31 then feeds an absolute manifest to a case titled 'an import given a relative manifest ... prints it absolute' and its assertion (isabs(words[2]) and samefile) is trivially true: the case is green on the one machine it was fixed for without exercising the relative-to-absolute conversion. The title now says 'relative here: False', but a title is not an assertion, and nothing makes a green run on that runner read as vacuous. The helper's docstring asks such a caller to check isabs and say so; this one says so only in text.
findings.resolution: Make the case exercise the relative spelling on every drive layout: run the CLI with the working directory moved into os.path.dirname(mp10) (os.chdir in try/finally, M.main runs in-process) and pass os.path.basename(mp10); then no cross-drive question exists. Failing that, assert the 'relative here' leg only when it is relative and record the absolute leg as a separate, honestly-titled case.

findings.issue: os.getcwd() is classified as neither scratch nor checkout, so the exact call the executor wrote to repair i31, relpath(scratch_path, os.getcwd()), is invisible to the new lint, while the one-argument spelling of the same thing is convicted (s30). The one-arg branch carries the comment that the working directory is the checkout when a suite is run by hand; the two-arg spelling of that same fact is a hole. A future relpath(mkdtemp(), os.getcwd()) goes unnamed.
findings.resolution: Treat a call to getcwd as a checkout-kind source in _path_kinds (or normalise relpath(x, getcwd()) to the one-argument rule), and add a planted case beside s30.
